title: Plugin and Tool Extension Runtime
summary: Provide governed, isolated and evidence-backed plugin and tool execution without unbounded code, network, data or credential access.

intent.statement: Extend AGASTYA through verified versioned plugins and tools while preserving policy, sandbox, secret and evidence boundaries.
desired_outcomes: Plugins are immutable, signed and approval-governed.
Every tool invocation receives an effective least-privilege grant.
Tools cannot bypass the Vault, Ledger or Agent Control Plane.

success_measures.name: Invocation provenance coverage
success_measures.target: 100% of tool invocations carry plugin digest, grant, correlation and evidence
success_measures.measurement_method: Reconcile runtime invocations with registry and ledger records.

success_measures.name: Default isolation
success_measures.target: 0 plugin host filesystem, raw secret, direct database or unallowlisted egress accesses
success_measures.measurement_method: Security integration tests and sandbox telemetry.

provenance.rationale: Safe extensibility required for AI-native engineering control plane.

problem.statement: Platform extensions can compromise security, tenant isolation and trustworthy evidence when packages, permissions, secrets and tool output are not governed by a common runtime.
problem.current_state: AGASTYA has agent, evidence and Vault foundations but no extension manifest, plugin trust, sandbox or versioned tool execution contract.
impact: Untrusted plugin code could escape platform policy.
Tool output could be mistaken for verified evidence.
Extensions could expose secrets or cross-project data.

business_context.business_value: The runtime creates a durable, controlled integration path rather than coupling AGASTYA to provider-specific tools or unsafe plugins.

stakeholders.name: Security Engineering
stakeholders.role: Approves trust, sandbox and capability policies

actors.name: Project Owner
goals: Approve project extension grants and lifecycle actions.

actors.name: Extension Registry
goals: Validate manifests, trust evidence and lifecycle state.

actors.name: Sandbox Runtime
goals: Run permitted tools in isolated resource-bounded execution.

actors.name: AI Agent
goals: Request a registered tool through orchestration policy.

functional_requirements.title: Register immutable extension manifests
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall register immutable PluginManifests and ToolDefinitions with publisher identity, digest/signature, version, contracts, capabilities, resource, egress and compatibility metadata.

functional_requirements.title: Validate trust before enablement
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall validate manifest, package integrity, publisher trust, scan evidence and policy before enabling a plugin or project extension grant.

functional_requirements.title: Execute only in isolated runtime
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall execute plugin tools only in an isolated runtime with explicit resource limits and no default host, database, network or secret access.

functional_requirements.title: Calculate effective invocation grants
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall calculate an effective invocation grant before each tool execution using project, environment, task, classification, tool, policy, secret and approval context.

functional_requirements.title: Broker agent tool invocation
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall route every agent-initiated tool call through registered schemas, policy evaluation, output controls and Evidence Ledger evidence.

provenance.rationale: Extension runtime cannot bypass control plane.

functional_requirements.title: Integrate opaque Vault leases
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall materialise credentials only through opaque Vault lease and registered execution boundary; plugin or model output must never include secret material.

functional_requirements.title: Govern extension version lifecycle
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall support enable, disable, upgrade, rollback, revoke and uninstall operations as governed versioned lifecycle events.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Plugin execution shall have no host filesystem, raw database, raw secret, process or network authority by default and shall enforce declared resource limits.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Sandbox security suite attempts undeclared filesystem, network, host and secret access while asserting denial and audit evidence.
non_functional_requirements.target: Zero successful undeclared capability accesses in the security suite.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Plugin disablement or revocation shall prevent new invocations immediately and record active-execution cancellation or safe-boundary outcome.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Integration tests revoke a version during queued and active invocations.

business_rules.statement: A plugin can be enabled only if its immutable manifest/digest, publisher, scan evidence, compatibility and required approval are valid.
Plugins receive no host filesystem, raw database, network, shell or secret access by default; only named capabilities in an effective invocation grant may be brokered.
An agent or plugin may not receive plaintext secret material; a registered execution boundary may materialise it only through an opaque short-lived Vault lease.

constraints.statement: Initial extension runtime supports signed internal, read-only plugin/tool packages only; third-party packages, persistent listeners, production write actions and external webhook receivers are excluded.
constraints.rationale: Trust and isolation controls must be demonstrated before broader extension authority.

dependencies.name: Sandbox execution environment
dependencies.risk: Sandbox technology and runtime deployment must satisfy isolation/resource requirements before execution implementation.

dependencies.name: Publisher trust and package scanning service
dependencies.risk: Publisher signing, SBOM and scan evidence policy must be chosen before unbuilt packages are accepted.

bounded_contexts.name: Extension Platform
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Own plugin manifests, tool definitions, publishers, effective grants, isolated invocation and lifecycle evidence.

ubiquitous_language.definition: Immutable declared contract for an extension package and its tools/capabilities.
Per-invocation least-privilege authority derived from project and runtime policy.
Isolated execution environment with default-deny host, data, egress and secret boundaries.

workflows.name: Invoke a registered read-only tool
workflows.trigger: An authorised user or agent task requests a compatible registered tool.

steps.action: Resolves immutable tool/plugin digest and confirms publisher, scan and enablement state.
steps.result: Invalid or revoked package is denied.

steps.action: Evaluates effective grant and validates input contract before execution.
steps.result: Invocation is denied, waits for approval or receives a bound grant.

steps.action: Runs tool in isolation and validates/redacts/classifies output.
steps.result: Bounded output/evidence is returned without raw secret exposure.

outcomes: Tool result is traceable to immutable package, policy and evidence.
workflows.error_handling: Schema, policy, resource, network, sandbox and secret violations deny/quarantine output and write containment evidence.

states.name: SUBMITTED
states.description: Manifest awaiting integrity and security validation.

states.name: UNINSTALLED
states.description: Version no longer available after retention policy.

security_requirements.statement: Plugin registration, grants and invocations shall enforce publisher/package trust, project scope, tool purpose, input/output schema, classification, effective capability and metadata-only audit evidence.
security_requirements.verification_method: Security suite covers unsigned/tampered package, cross-project call, undeclared capability, secret exposure and output redaction fixtures.

observability_requirements.statement: Plugin lifecycle, grant, invocation, resource, egress, output, policy and containment outcomes shall emit structured correlated ledger events.
observability_requirements.verification_method: End-to-end tests reconstruct one invocation from manifest digest to evidence record.

acceptance_criteria.title: Unverified package is not enabled
acceptance_criteria.given: A signed internal package with manifest and scan evidence.
acceptance_criteria.then: The registry stores immutable metadata but enables it only after policy and approval requirements complete.

acceptance_criteria.title: Undeclared capabilities are denied
acceptance_criteria.given: A plugin requests host, filesystem, database, network or secret authority outside grant.
acceptance_criteria.when: Runtime processes execution or broker request.
acceptance_criteria.then: Access is denied before use and containment evidence is written.

acceptance_criteria.title: Read-only tool invocation is governed
acceptance_criteria.given: An approved read-only ToolDefinition and valid input.
acceptance_criteria.then: Execution preserves digest, grant, correlation and bounded evidence.

acceptance_criteria.title: Secret-backed call preserves agent blindness
acceptance_criteria.given: A policy-permitted secret-backed registered tool action.
acceptance_criteria.then: Agent receives no plaintext and tool receives only opaque Vault lease at execution boundary.

acceptance_criteria.title: Revocation contains pending and active work
acceptance_criteria.given: A plugin version is revoked during queued or active execution.
acceptance_criteria.then: New work is denied and active work records safe cancellation or escalation outcome.

acceptance_criteria.title: Unsafe tool output is withheld
acceptance_criteria.given: A result violates schema, size or secret-redaction policy.
acceptance_criteria.then: Output is rejected/quarantined/redacted and is not returned unsafely.

test_requirements.scope: Manifest, signature/digest, scan evidence and approval enablement path.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Immutable registry record and denied/approved lifecycle evidence.

test_requirements.scope: Sandbox default-deny filesystem, process, data, egress and secret capability suite.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Denied access attempts with containment events.

test_requirements.scope: Policy-approved read-only invocation with input/output contracts and evidence.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Invocation record carrying digest, grant, correlation and output hash.

test_requirements.scope: Opaque Vault lease at registered tool execution boundary.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Agent/task/log fixtures prove no secret plaintext; tool lease trace proves scope/TTL binding.
Version lifecycle and active invocation outcome trace.

test_requirements.scope: Output schema, size, classification and secret-redaction quarantine.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Withheld output and safe evidence event.

risks.title: Sandbox escape or overbroad capability grant
risks.description: An extension runtime weakness could expose host, tenant data or secrets.
risks.mitigation: Default-deny sandbox, named brokered capabilities, runtime ADR, security testing and read-only internal initial scope.

open_questions.question: Which sandbox technology and execution infrastructure meet internal runtime isolation and resource requirements?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Plugin execution infrastructure cannot be safely implemented.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a detailed-design risk. Sandbox technology and runtime ADR are mandatory before any plugin execution.

open_questions.question: What publisher trust tiers, signing process and vulnerability scan evidence are mandatory for package registration?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Unbuilt package acceptance and third-party onboarding cannot be defined.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a detailed-design risk. Publisher trust, signing and scan policy are mandatory gates before any package onboarding.

architecture_decisions.title: Use isolated default-deny extension execution with brokered capabilities
architecture_decisions.context: Extensions require useful integrations without host-level authority or bypass of policy/vault/ledger boundaries.
architecture_decisions.decision: Run plugin tools in isolated resource-bounded runtimes and grant only named capabilities through existing policy, Vault and evidence brokers.

alternatives.name: In-process extension modules
alternatives.summary: Load plugin code into the AGASTYA application process.
alternatives.rejection_reason: Exposes host process, dependencies and tenant data to untrusted extension code.

alternatives.name: Unrestricted container execution
alternatives.summary: Run package with broad filesystem and network capability.
alternatives.rejection_reason: Cannot enforce least privilege or produce trustworthy capability evidence.

architecture_decisions.rationale: Default-deny isolation plus typed brokers preserves AGASTYA control-plane authority.
consequences: Sandbox/runtime selection is a mandatory ADR gate.
Initial extension support is constrained to signed read-only internal tools.

provenance.rationale: Tool invocation must remain governed by the agent control plane.
Plugins must obey secure opaque secret materialisation.
